themes.label: Leadership rotation, not rollover
themes.narrative: The market reads Mag7 weakness as healthy broadening: the index holds near its highs while leadership rotates, so the bull case is intact.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 names average -12.19% from their 52-week highs vs SPY at -2.4% — a -9.79pt divergence gap (AAPL strongest at -1.3%, TSLA weakest at -28.9%). Credit does not confirm stress: SLOOS lending standards are 0% (LOOSE, far below the ~40% stress zone) and HY OAS is 3.23.
themes.counterRead: Rotation is real at the top but it is not broadening downward: IWM is -1.90% today, -5.45% on the month and -8.7% over 3 months, and the VIX jumped +21.39% today to 19.98 (+29.4% on the month). Index calm is masking churn underneath, and the divergence becomes a rollover signal if credit flips from loose.
themes.watchFor: SLOOS tightening off 0% or HY OAS pushing through 4% would convert this rotation read into a rollover read.

themes.label: Restrictive real rates into the FOMC
themes.narrative: After the Sep CPI event (Oct 14, HIGH signal) and a hot PPI read, the market narrative is a Fed with no room to ease — rate-hike jitters drove Friday's Nasdaq-led selloff (QQQ -2.77% vs SPY -1.36%).
themes.dataAnchor: The constraint is real rates, not inflation expectations: 10Y at 5.10%, 30Y at 5.44%, real 10Y at 2.75% while breakeven inflation is only 2.35%. The curve is positive (2s10s +0.33) with DFF at 3.88 and the 2Y at 4.77, and the next decision point is the FOMC on Oct 27-28.
themes.counterRead: Credit is not validating a policy-error spiral: HY OAS at 3.23 is calm and the curve is bear-steepening in an orderly way, not disorderly. Duration multiples are being repriced, but nothing in the credit data says the tightening is breaking borrowers yet.
themes.watchFor: A 10Y sustained above ~5.25-5.5% or HY OAS widening through 4% into the Oct 27-28 FOMC changes the posture from selective to defensive.

themes.label: AI-infra quality dislocation
themes.narrative: The tape narrative treats AI infrastructure as a spent trade: the whole complex was sold Friday regardless of fundamentals, and the screen's declines are tagged sentiment-driven, not thesis-driven.
themes.dataAnchor: AVGO is -33.6% from its high with revenue growing +55% YoY, 67.8% gross margin and $26.9B FCF (top-conviction score 82, Tier A). NVDA is only -12% from peak with revenue +61.4% YoY (conviction promotion, score 82, RSI 37.5). VRT is -45.7% from its high with revenue +27.7% and RSI 27.3. All three carry FULL_SIGNAL dislocations with SENTIMENT_DRIVEN decline tags.
themes.counterRead: Fundamentals are ahead of price here, which is the DATA_AHEAD setup — but it is a research queue, not a buy list: the pullback posture is RESEARCH_SCREENED (verify thesis before sizing), several names in the same screen (APP -63.9%, KTOS -69.8%) show how far sentiment unwinds can run, and a 5.10% 10Y keeps compressing the multiples these names re-rate on.
themes.watchFor: Earnings confirmation of the revenue lines (AVGO +55%, NVDA +61.4%) against the drawdowns, and any revenue-inflection flip from RECOVERY to DETERIORATING, decides whether the dislocation is opportunity or value trap.

themes.label: Speculative nuclear/space unwind
themes.narrative: The AI-power and space complex was priced as the next guaranteed leg of the build-out — headline catalysts like Vistra's $4.2B federal loan kept the story bid long after the prices detached from near-term cash flows.
themes.dataAnchor: The 1-month laggard list is dominated by this complex: SMR -36.08%, ASTS -35.18%, OKLO -29.72%, RKLB -24.87%, URA -16.96%, CCJ -11.84% — and Friday accelerated it (ASTS -8.57%, OKLO -7.15%, SMR -6.04% on the day). Even the quality name in the theme, VST, is -26% from its high despite a +5.18% month and $1.17M of insider buying at the trough.
themes.counterRead: This is the narrative-ahead complex deflating while the actual power-demand data (data-center load, the VST loan) hasn't changed — the unwind is about positioning and multiple, not the underlying electricity story. That distinction matters: it argues against chasing the bounce and against shorting the quality name (VST) with the speculative ones.
themes.watchFor: A stabilization where SMR/OKLO stop making new monthly lows while VST holds its insider-buy zone would mark the unwind exhausting; continued -7% days say it has further to run.

themes.label: Defensive rails leadership
themes.narrative: Quietly, the market is paying for cash-flow rails over duration: payment networks and quality compounders are the month's leadership while growth duration sells off.
themes.dataAnchor: MA is the #1 tracked leader at +8.89% on the month and was essentially flat Friday (-0.05%) against SPY -1.36% and QQQ -2.77%. KNSL screens at -21.1% from its high with revenue +18%, 26.9% FCF margin and RSI 62.5 — relative strength, not distress. IBIT is +6.56% on the month as the other non-duration bid.
themes.counterRead: Rails leadership is a defensive tell, not a bullish one: capital is hiding in toll-takers because the 10Y at 5.10% makes long-duration cash flows expensive. If real yields back off after the FOMC, this leadership likely underperforms the rebound — own it as ballast, not as the growth engine.
themes.watchFor: MA losing its relative-strength line (a down month vs SPY) or the 10Y breaking below ~4.9% would signal the defensive rotation is ending.

strategyPosture: Stay selective and research-first into the weekend: SPY -1.36% and QQQ -2.77% on Friday with VIX 19.98 argue against chasing, while DATA_AHEAD dislocations in AVGO, VRT and NVDA warrant thesis verification under the RESEARCH_SCREENED pullback posture, not automatic sizing. Credit (HY OAS 3.23, SLOOS 0% LOOSE) gives no rollover confirmation to de-risk on.
whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds around the Oct 27-28 FOMC and the real-rate path: a 10Y pushing through ~5.25-5.5% or HY OAS cracking 4% turns rotation into rollover, while a calm FOMC lets the AI-infra dislocation (AVGO/NVDA/VRT) become the re-entry queue.
watchFor: HY OAS widening through 4% (from 3.23) — the rotation-to-rollover trigger
10Y sustained above ~5.25-5.5% or a break below ~4.9% after the Oct 27-28 FOMC
Mag7-vs-SPY divergence gap widening past ~12pts (from -9.79pts) or SLOOS tightening off 0%
VIX closing above ~25 (from 19.98) or IWM stabilizing against SPY after -8.7% over 3 months
Earnings verification of AVGO (+55% YoY) and NVDA (+61.4% YoY) revenue against their -33.6% / -12% drawdowns
